neighbours.label: digits of a converted measurement in parentheses after the original value (e.g. '(214°F', '(819-mi)')
fire: The summit of the volcano reaches 3,776 m (12,388 ft) above sea level.
Set the oven to 220°C (428°F) and roast the vegetables for half an hour.
The new rail line covers 1,150 km (715 mi) between the two capitals.
On the hottest day the thermometer showed 46°C (115°F) in the shade.
The dam holds back a reservoir that is 85 km (53 mi) long and very deep.
Engine output was raised to 450 hp (336 kW) in the final production model.
The tower stands 324 m (1,063 ft) tall and was finished in 1889.
Hikers should carry at least 3 litres (101 fl oz) of water per person.
quiet: The summit of the volcano reaches 3,776 metres above sea level on clear days.
Set the oven to its highest setting and roast the vegetables for half an hour.
The new rail line covers 1,150 kilometres between the two capitals in total.
On the hottest day the thermometer showed a record 46 degrees in the shade.
The dam holds back a reservoir that is about 85 kilometres long and very deep.
Engine output was raised to 450 horsepower in the final production model.
The tower stands 324 metres tall and was finished in the year 1889.
Hikers should carry at least three litres of water per person on the trail.

notes: Card: top peaks are leading digits of the second value in a metric/imperial conversion, plus some numbers in code lists. Quiet items keep the same numbers and topics without a parenthetical conversion.
